slides.heading: Booleans
slides.body: Booleans is part of Variables and Primitive Data Types. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Booleans
slides.body: A boolean stores only one of two values: True or False. Booleans are important for decisions and conditions.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: A boolean is like a light switch. It is either on or off, True or False.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Use clear variable names and match the data type to the kind of value you need to store.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Create a boolean variable named is_ready with the value True and print it.
slides.hint: Remember that True starts with a capital T in Python.

coding_challenge.prompt_text: Create a boolean variable named passed with the value False and print it.
coding_challenge.hint_text: Use the idea from the lesson. Keep the code short, readable, and correctly indented.
